answers.text:
Answer for the calling agent — grounded against the currently-served release.

## 1. A cloned bot's OPEN POSITIONS

- First resolve the bot: MCP `get_my_clones` → returns your clones with their `instance_id` and status. (REST twin: `GET /api/v1/cloned-bots`.)
- Open positions: MCP `get_positions`. It returns the account's currently-open positions; each row carries a `source` field of `"clone"` (an open clone-bot trade) or `"wta"` (a prediction-market bet), so to see one bot's positions filter the `"clone"` rows for that `instance_id`.
- Executed/closed history for the same bot: MCP `get_order_history`.

There is no separate "positions-for-one-clone" MCP verb — you scope the account positions by the clone's `instance_id`/`source`.

## 2. Its LOCKED balance

- MCP `get_clone_balance` with `{ "instance_id": "<id>" }`. It returns, for that single clone, its balance, its `locked_in_trades`, and `available` (= balance − locked), plus a state marker that reads `OPEN_STAKES` when anything is locked and `NONE` when nothing is.
- REST twin: `GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/balance`.
- A fresh clone is PAUSED with 0 balance until `fund_clone_bot` runs; a paper clone is funded from the account's simulated balance, a live clone from real USDC.

## 3. Where `locked_in_trades` comes from

It is **computed live at read time, not a stored field.** On each balance read the server sums the committed notional/stake of that clone's currently-*open* trades and subtracts it from the clone's balance to produce `available` (clamped at ≥ 0). So `locked_in_trades` = the capital that clone has tied up in open positions right now; it drops back to 0 as those positions close. This is the exact figure surfaced as "Locked" on the my-bots view and in the bot-withdraw modal (withdrawable = balance − locked). For a paper clone it reflects simulated open-trade locks and never rolls into the account's real total balance.

## 4. Where the "activity feed" comes from

Distinguish three things — don't conflate them:

- **The bot's own activity (its trades):** the user-scoped activity/P&L feed merges clone trades (`source="clone"`) with WTA bets (`source="wta"`) into one recent-activity/positions list. For an agent, reach the executed side via MCP `get_order_history` and the open side via MCP `get_positions`; the full paginated per-user activity/positions/P&L list is served over the account/profile REST surface (`GET /api/v1/users/.../activity`, positions and P&L endpoints under the user-profile API).
- **Live per-clone events (stop-loss / take-profit fires, SL-TP lifecycle):** streamed over the clone-bot-events WebSocket at `ws://<host>/ws/clone-bot-events?token=<JWT>`, fanned out from the platform's internal `clone_bot` SL/TP event channels. This is the real-time push feed for one owner's clones; it is JWT-authed, not an MCP verb.
- **The public aggregate bot-activity ticker** (market-wide agent trades, unique-trader counts across all perpetual agent instances) is a *separate, public* feed and is NOT your bot's own activity — do not read per-clone state from it.

Net: to inspect one clone programmatically, `get_my_clones` → `get_clone_balance` (locked/available) + `get_positions` (open) + `get_order_history` (executed); for a live push of that clone's SL/TP events use the clone-bot-events WebSocket. `locked_in_trades` is derived on the fly from that clone's open trades, not a persisted balance.

Here is a concrete, evidence-backed paper strategy for the ~89,000 USDC bankroll. Everything below uses only cards I confirmed **live and `tradeable_now: true` in this run** via `get_event_card_info`, and every number is drawn from tool output cited in the "Evidence" section — not memory.

## First, a structural finding that shapes the whole strategy
The event-card deck right now is **not as diversified as the titles suggest**. Of the live cards I pulled, five are dominated by two crypto legs:

- `f197d20f-…` "Bitcoin Selling Pressure Drops…" → basket is **~99.6% BTC**
- `8eaedadc-…` "MARA Stock…" → **~99.99% Bitcoin Cash (BCH)**
- `4c624693-…` "iPhone 18…" → **~99.95% BCH**
- `90fd8212-…` "Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP…" → **~99.4% BCH**
- `e579581b-…` "Pepeto DeFi…" → **68.5% BCH / 31.5% OKB**
- `87ccf8f3-…` "SAIB: CRWV — CoreWeave" → **100% CRWV stock**, open-ended

So cards 2–5 are effectively **the same BCH position wearing different headlines**. Stacking them is one bet in disguise, not diversification — I use exactly one BCH card. The only genuinely uncorrelated live leg is the CoreWeave equity card.

Also important: the lower index levels on the iPhone/XRP/Pepeto cards (~91.7, ~91.7, ~92.2) reflect **when they were minted**, not a discount. A `/buy` now buys the underlying (BCH) at today's price regardless of the index reading — do **not** treat "index at 92" as "buy the dip."

## The strategy (execute now, paper=true)

`POST /api/v1/event-cards/{card_id}/buy` opens a **long (trade-up)** position — that endpoint is long-only. Sizes are fractions of the 89,000 bankroll.

| Card id | What it really is | Side | Fraction | ≈ USDC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `f197d20f-db76-431d-a10c-75a538ebe213` | ~99.6% BTC | BUY (long / up) | **30%** | ~26,700 |
| `8eaedadc-229b-4d1b-8d1e-7ea74ac5bae2` | ~99.99% BCH | BUY (long / up) | **12%** | ~10,680 |
| — reserve / dry powder — | | hold | **58%** | ~51,620 |

Deploy ~42% and keep 58% in reserve, because (a) BTC and BCH are highly correlated crypto beta — book risk does not scale like √N here — and (b) both cards close in ~2 days, so the opportunity to redeploy comes fast.

**Do NOT buy right now:** `87ccf8f3-…` (CoreWeave). It's the only diversifier, but its **MACD is bearish** (macd −0.38 below signal +0.80, histogram −1.18). If you want a non-crypto leg, wait for its MACD histogram to cross positive, then a `/buy` of ≤8% (~7,120). It's open-ended (`trading_closes_at: null`), so there's no time pressure. A trade-**down** on it cannot be done through `/buy` — you'd use the MCP tool `trade_event_card` with the sell/bear side.

## When to close
